resolution: The phase breakdown proved the loader JS is clean (scans=0, push=0) but revealed a compounding multi-second host-block (1016ms→3021ms, growing per edit) — and the requestAnimationFrame 'rendered' proxy batches under that saturation (identical repeated host-block values, pre inheriting the prior line's block), so the absolute host-block is backlog not a clean per-edit cost. To get ground truth on WHAT is blocking the main thread, folded the host's own per-frame telemetry into the edit-latency line: exported readFrameRecord/readCounters from perfWatch and appended 'host DOMINANT=<phase> tick/paint/gpu ms | nodes N inst I draws D meshes M'. Since V8 runs on the host thread, a long JS block surfaces as huge tickUs; a GPU re-upload as gpuUs; CPU raster as paintUs — and if the scene counts CLIMB per edit the compounding is a leak (nodes/instances accumulating) rather than a fixed cost. One place-click now classifies the bottleneck. Cart-side, hot-reloads. Sha caffa8071. Next: read the host line, then go kill the dominant phase (JS path vs GPU upload vs a node/instance leak).
